channel.title: nexusEVnews
channel.description: Independent EV and renewable energy news, curated daily. Electric vehicles, solar, battery tech, and charging infrastructure.

item.title: The Zero-Resistance Motor Designed for Aviation Is Already Working. Data Centers Are First.
item.dc:creator: Ziroth
item.description: Hinetics has built a superconducting motor that achieves 40 kW per kg at 99.5% efficiency by eliminating resistance entirely from the rotor electromagnets. The key engineering insight is a Stirling cycle cooling engine embedded in the spinning rotor itself. Baby Yoda, their proof-of-concept prototype, has logged hundreds of hours of testing and the first commercial target is generators for data centers, not aircraft.

item.title: The Lucid Air Touring Starts at $81,400 and Has Almost No Real Competition
item.dc:creator: Driving With Jonny
item.description: Johnny reviews the Touring trim of the Lucid Air: 620 hp, 885 lb-ft of torque, a drag coefficient of 0.21, and an interior that competes with cars costing twice as much. The Touring drops two battery packs from the standard model and shifts from 924 to 756 volts, but the torque figure and range around 460 miles hold up well at the $81,400 starting price.

item.title: CATL's Sodium Battery Is 65% Cheaper Than LFP at Cell Level. The Pack Math Is More Complicated.
item.dc:creator: Ben Alexxander
item.description: CATL's next-generation sodium-ion cell is currently $19 per kilowatt-hour at cell level, against $55 to $65 for LFP at comparable scale. Lifespan is claimed at 3.6 million miles before 85% capacity. Energy density has reached 175 Wh/kg. At pack level with cooling and electronics, the cost rises to around $40 to $45 per kilowatt-hour, but scaling on existing LFP production lines is possible within 12 to 24 months.

item.title: First Time Inside the R2: Better Storage, Cushier Seats, Fewer Compromises Than the R1
item.dc:creator: Tailosive EV
item.description: Tailosive EV gets hands-on with the Rivian R2 at a show event alongside an R1S. The seats are noticeably cushier, there are two deep glove boxes, a built-in magnetic charger, and ambient lighting extending to the rear doors. The second row is genuinely comfortable for longer trips. The audio system drew the only clear criticism in an otherwise strong first impression.

item.title: Formula E Gen4 Has 600 kW, Permanent Four-Wheel Drive, and Opens What Manufacturers Can Learn
item.dc:creator: FIA / Formula E
item.description: The FIA's Gen4 Formula E car delivers 600 kW in qualifying and 700 kW of regenerative braking. It is the first single-seater racing car with permanent four-wheel drive. Manufacturers now have full freedom to develop their own traction control, brake-by-wire, and torque distribution systems, with explicit intent to transfer that knowledge to production road cars.

item.title: Rivian's New AI Can Change Your Drive Mode, Read Your Texts, and Submit Bug Reports
item.dc:creator: RivianTrackr
item.description: Rivian Assistant runs on Google Gemini and does what no other production in-car AI currently does: it controls the vehicle. Drive mode, ride height, seat heat, SMS replies, navigation with charging stops. It also needs a $15 monthly subscription, can't adjust your charge limit, and won't touch the wipers. RivianTrackr spent 25 minutes breaking it.

item.title: 226 hp, 441L Boot, and More Character Than the ID Polo Will Ever Have
item.dc:creator: Electrifying
item.description: The CUPRA Raval shares its platform with the ID Polo but adds an e-LSD, launch control, a 15mm-lower suspension, and a boot bigger than a Golf. Starting from £23,785. The VZ does 0-62 in 6.8 seconds and makes Barcelona rush hour feel interesting. Electrifying drove it, and the steering is still too light.

item.title: Four Anker Solix Batteries, Three Months, and Almost No Savings. Here's Why.
item.dc:creator: Everyday Chris
item.description: The Anker Solix E10 does everything it says: discharges during peak rates, recharges overnight, switches over in 20 milliseconds when the grid drops. The problem is no solar. Without panels charging the batteries for free during the day, the math barely pencils out. And nobody in Orange County will install panels on an HOA roof.

item.title: Five Aptera Vehicles Off the Line. 50,000 Reservations Are Waiting.
item.dc:creator: Aptera
item.description: Aptera has completed five vehicles on its 14-station Carlsbad validation line and documented cycle time improvements with each successive build. The fleet will expand into a full testing program covering road performance, safety, software, and solar energy collection. No production start date has been announced.

item.title: BYD Starts Below $12,000. China Is Near 70% of Global EV Sales. The US Has a 100% Tariff.
item.dc:creator: NBC News
item.description: NBC News drove a BYD in China. Massage seats, autonomous parking, sub-$12,000 price point. The US blocks all Chinese EVs with a 100% tariff, which keeps the comparison theoretical but doesn't stop the videos from going viral. China is approaching 70% of all EVs sold globally.

item.title: Infinite Machine's Alto Wants to Fill the Gap Between an E-Bike and a Vespa
item.dc:creator: InsideEVs
item.description: A New York startup built a class-3 electric scooter that needs no plates and no insurance in most states. It does 28 mph, has full suspension and a removable 1.2 kWh battery, and a GPS chip that keeps transmitting even after you pull the battery out. InsideEVs spent a week riding it around Manhattan, including leaving it outside for five days.

item.title: Hammond Drove the NIO ES9 Around Shanghai. The Suspension Was What Surprised Him Most.
item.dc:creator: Everything Electric APAC
item.description: NIO puts tiny hydraulic pumps directly at each wheel rather than routing pressure from a central unit. On Belgian paving stones at speed, the only evidence you're on them is the sound. A crowdsourced pothole database shared across every NIO vehicle pre-arms the suspension before the rough surface arrives.

item.title: The PV5 Starts at £31,495 After the UK EV Grant. The ID.Buzz Starts at £60,000. Electrifying Drove Both.
item.dc:creator: Electrifying
item.description: More boot space, a V2L socket, regen paddles, and one-pedal driving at roughly half the price. Both reviewers chose the Kia. The Buzz wins on power, range, electric sliding doors, and cabin quality. Neither is a bad choice, but the £27,000 gap makes one of them much easier to justify.

item.title: Xiaomi Hired Engineers From BMW, Porsche, and Lamborghini. EU Entry Is Second Half 2027.
item.dc:creator: Out of Spec Roaming
item.description: Fifty engineers in a Munich R&D centre. One ran the BMW M4 GT3 race programme. One tuned the 3 Series, Z4, and X5 chassis. One designed the exterior of the Porsche 992 GT3 RS. Another led the AMG Vision GT. Xiaomi has delivered over 400,000 vehicles and is targeting half a million in 2026.

item.title: The BMW iX3 Gets to Yorkshire First, But the Tesla Costs a Third Less to Charge
item.dc:creator: What Car?
item.description: What Car? drives the BMW iX3 and Tesla Model Y on a 500-mile London-to-Yorkshire round trip. The iX3 arrived first, logged real-world range of around 393 miles, and averaged 170 kW charging. The Tesla charged at 129 kW on average and cost £36 less to run over the full trip on Supercharger pricing.

item.title: Two Batteries, One Hitch, and the Case for All-Electric Glamping
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: The Lightship AE1 carries its own 69 kWh battery and 80 kW motor to neutralize trailer drag on the tow vehicle. Paired with a Rivian, the real-world efficiency numbers are hard to argue with. This is what all-electric glamping looks like when the hardware actually works.

item.title: Atlanta, Rivian, and the Quiet Coincidence
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: Atlanta has a failing air quality grade and a Rivian plant on its doorstep. A hypothetical about what one city could do with the electric mobility infrastructure that already exists — R2 autonomous taxis, ALSO cargo quads, e-bikes, and ZTL-style restricted zones — and what the health data says the stakes actually are. Includes data from the HEI lockdown air quality study (Chen et al., 2025) and the American Lung Association's 2025 Atlanta air quality report.
